story_type: lift boat on steel legs sprays water on a burning shrimp boat offshore, three people picked up
hook: A shrimp boat caught fire. A lift boat came to fight it.
narration: Ten miles off Galveston, a shrimp boat was on fire, and a lift boat was spraying water right into it.
The lift boat A.J. Burios had called the Coast Guard around nine that morning.
Three people were aboard the burning shrimp boat, the Master Ryan.
A lift boat jacks itself up on tall steel legs, which turns it into a work platform out at sea.
Its crew kept the water on the Master Ryan as white smoke poured off the deck.
The Coast Guard sent a Dolphin helicopter, a forty seven foot motor lifeboat and the cutter Manowar.
A pleasure boat named High Pressure picked up all three people from the Master Ryan.
outcome: A Coast Guard motor lifeboat then carried all three to Station Galveston.
title: Lift boat fights a burning shrimp boat
description:
The Coast Guard responded to a fire aboard the fishing vessel Master Ryan 10 miles off Galveston, Texas, on Dec. 6, 2008, after the lift boat A.J. Burios reported the fire with three people aboard. The pleasure craft High Pressure recovered the three, and a Coast Guard 47-foot motor lifeboat took them to Station Galveston.
